question:
Identify the spelling error in the given sentence.

The restaurant offered a diverse menu with a wide renge of culinary options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. renge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "renge" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "range", meaning a variety or selection of things. (श्रेणी / विविधता)

◦ Correct: The restaurant offered a diverse menu with a wide range of culinary options.

• Spelling key: R + A + N + G + E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "restaurant", "diverse" and "options" are all spelt correctly in the sentence.

• "restaurant" is a commonly misspelt word — note the silent "au" and the ending "-rant".

NOTE

• "Range" as a noun means an extent/variety (a wide range of options); as a verb it means to vary between limits (prices range from ₹10 to ₹100).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The charismatic leader's speeches were known for their __________ impact on motivating people to take positive actions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. profound.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Profound" means very great, deep or intense. A "profound impact" is a deep, far-reaching effect, which fits speeches that strongly motivate people. (गहरा / प्रगाढ़)

◦ Correct: ... known for their profound impact on motivating people to take positive actions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "frugal" (economical, thrifty) describes spending, not impact.

• Option 3 "doldrums" (a state of inactivity or depression) is a noun and does not fit.

• Option 4 "impenitence" (lack of remorse) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of profound: deep, intense, far-reaching, significant. Antonyms: superficial, shallow, trivial.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Kumbh Mela (the festival of the sacred Pitcher) is the world's biggest peaceful gathering of pilgrims, with participants bathing or taking the dip in the _____ river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sacred.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sacred" means holy, religious or revered. Pilgrims at the Kumbh Mela take a dip in the sacred (holy) river, so the word fits the religious context. (पवित्र)

◦ Correct: ... with participants bathing or taking the dip in the sacred river.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "depth" is a noun and cannot describe the river here as an adjective.

• Option 2 "profane" (irreligious, secular) is the opposite of sacred.

• Option 4 "shallow" (not deep) does not suit the reverent tone.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sacred: holy, hallowed, blessed, divine, revered. Antonyms: profane, secular, unholy.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the given sentence.

She runs very quick in marathons.
option_1: She run very quick in marathons.
option_2: She runs very quickly in marathons.
option_3: She run much quickly in marathons.
option_4: She runs much quickly in marathons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. She runs very quickly in marathons.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word describing the verb "runs" must be an adverb, not an adjective. The adverb of "quick" is "quickly". So it should be "runs very quickly".

◦ Correct: She runs very quickly in marathons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 and Option 3 wrongly use "run" — with the singular subject "She", the verb must be "runs".

• "much" (Options 3, 4) is used with comparatives, not with the positive adverb here, so "very" is correct.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner modify verbs and usually end in "-ly": quick → quickly, slow → slowly, happy → happily. Use "very" (not "much") before a positive adjective/adverb.

question: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
option_1: The old lady broke down when she heard her son lost his job.
option_2: Try your level best before you decide to give up.
option_3: Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.
option_4: Clean out the backyard this weekend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb for arranging a bed is "make up the bed" (or simply "make the bed"), not "make over". "Make over" means to transform/renovate or to transfer ownership, which does not fit a daily bed-making habit.

◦ Correct: Make up the bed daily. It is a good habit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "broke down" (lost emotional control) is used correctly.

• Option 2 "give up" (to quit/stop trying) is correct.

• Option 4 "clean out" (to clean thoroughly / empty and clean) is correct.

NOTE

• "Make up" = to prepare/arrange (make up a bed), to invent (make up a story), to reconcile. "Make over" = to remodel or hand over.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in present perfect continuous tense form.

Rama is working on this project.
option_1: Rama has been working on this project since six months.
option_2: Rama has worked on this project for six months
option_3: Rama is working on this project for six months.
option_4: Rama has been working on this project for six months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rama has been working on this project for six months.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect continuous tense is formed with "has/have been + verb-ing". With a period of time, we use the preposition "for". So "has been working ... for six months" is correct.

◦ Correct: Rama has been working on this project for six months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "since" with a period (six months); "since" is used with a point of time, not a duration.

• Option 2 "has worked" is present perfect (simple), not continuous.

• Option 3 "is working ... for six months" is present continuous, which cannot show a six-month duration.

NOTE

• Rule: use "for" with a length of time (for six months, for two years) and "since" with a starting point (since June, since 2020).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack heavy / with supplies for the journey.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He climbed of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "climbed" is used without the preposition "of" here — one climbs "up" a trail or simply "climbs the trail". So "climbed of" is grammatically wrong; it should be "He climbed up" or "He climbed".

◦ Correct: He climbed the steep mountain trail, his backpack heavy with supplies for the journey.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "the steep mountain trail," "his backpack heavy" and "with supplies for the journey" are all grammatically correct.

• "his backpack heavy with supplies" is a correct absolute (nominative absolute) phrase.

NOTE

• Prepositions with "climb": climb up a hill, climb down a ladder, climb over a wall. "Climb of" is not a valid combination.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word.

Fragile
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Brittle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fragile" means easily broken or damaged; delicate. Its closest meaning/synonym is "brittle" (hard but easily broken). (नाज़ुक / भंगुर)

◦ Example: The fragile/brittle glass shattered on the floor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Florid" (very ornate / red-faced), Option 2 "Juicy" and Option 3 "Strong" do not match.

• Option 3 "Strong" is actually an antonym of fragile.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fragile: brittle, delicate, frail, breakable, flimsy. Antonyms: strong, sturdy, robust, tough.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Lisa was very excited about her promotion; she was very happy and delighted.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on cloud nine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on cloud nine" means extremely happy or elated, which perfectly replaces "very happy and delighted". (अत्यधिक प्रसन्न)

◦ Correct: Lisa was very excited about her promotion; she was on cloud nine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "on the ball" (alert and competent), Option 2 "on the attack" (attacking) and Option 4 "under the weather" (feeling unwell) do not express great happiness.

NOTE

• Idioms of joy: "on cloud nine", "over the moon", "on top of the world", "in seventh heaven", "walking on air".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

The author's writing was so captivating that readers were enthralled by every word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fascinated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enthralled" means captivated, spellbound or deeply interested. Its closest synonym is "fascinated". (मंत्रमुग्ध)

◦ Correct: ... readers were fascinated by every word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "jaded" (tired/bored from overuse), Option 2 "annoyed" (irritated) and Option 4 "bored" are all opposite in sense to being enthralled.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enthralled: fascinated, captivated, spellbound, mesmerised, engrossed. Antonyms: bored, uninterested, indifferent.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Brought to light
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To disclose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "brought to light" means to reveal, expose or make something known (that was hidden). Its meaning matches "to disclose". (उजागर करना / प्रकट करना)

◦ Example: The investigation brought to light several irregularities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To seem likely", Option 2 "To burn" and Option 3 "In favour of" do not convey the sense of revealing hidden information.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "come to light" (to become known), "shed light on" (to explain/clarify), "in the limelight" (in public attention).

question:
Select the option that can be used as one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Detailed examination of something complex
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Analysis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Analysis" means a detailed examination of the elements or structure of something, especially something complex. (विश्लेषण)

◦ Example: The scientist carried out a careful analysis of the data.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dialysis" (purification of blood in the kidney/machine), Option 2 "Synthesis" (combining parts into a whole) and Option 3 "Symbiosis" (mutual dependence between organisms) have different meanings.

• "Analysis" is the opposite of "synthesis".

NOTE

• Analysis (breaking down) vs Synthesis (building up). Plural of analysis is "analyses".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A dime a dozen
option_4: To be in a difficult situation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Very common.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a dime a dozen" means something very common and of little value / easily available. (बहुत आम / सस्ता और सामान्य)

◦ Example: Cheap souvenirs like these are a dime a dozen near tourist spots.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "Very rare", 3 "To take revenge" and 4 "To be in a difficult situation" do not match the meaning of being common and cheap.

NOTE

• A "dime" is a small US coin (10 cents); getting a dozen for a dime implies something plentiful and inexpensive.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Illicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Illegal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illicit" means forbidden by law, rules or custom; not allowed. Its closest synonym is "illegal". (अवैध / गैर-कानूनी)

◦ Example: The police seized a large quantity of illicit/illegal drugs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Integral" (essential/necessary), Option 3 "Inessential" (not necessary) and Option 4 "Inaugural" (relating to a beginning/opening) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "illicit" (unlawful) with "elicit" (to draw out a response). Synonyms of illicit: illegal, unlawful, prohibited, banned. Antonyms: legal, lawful, licit.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

"The architekture of the building is marvellous", said the spectators.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Architekture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Architekture" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "architecture" (with a "c", not a "k"), meaning the art/style of designing and constructing buildings. (वास्तुकला)

◦ Correct: The architecture of the building is marvellous.

• Spelling key: ARCHI + TEC + TURE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Marvellous" (British spelling with double "l"), "Spectators" and "Building" are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Related words: architect (a person who designs buildings), architectural (adjective), architecture (noun). Note the "ch" pronounced as /k/.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank.

Averted

Rohit ______ looking at Sheena's face while we were talking about domestic violence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. avoided.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Averted" means turned away / prevented / avoided. In the sentence, Rohit "averted" (avoided/turned away from) looking at Sheena's face, so the synonym is "avoided". (टाल दिया / नज़र फेर ली)

◦ Correct: Rohit avoided looking at Sheena's face while we were talking about domestic violence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "saw" and Option 3 "confronted" (faced directly) are opposite in sense here.

• Option 4 "fostered" (encouraged/nurtured) is unrelated.

NOTE

• "Avert" has two senses: (1) to turn away (avert one's eyes/gaze) and (2) to prevent (avert a disaster). Synonyms: avoid, prevent, ward off, turn away.

question:
Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank.

They may vary and seem very different, but they are not ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. irreconcilable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "irreconcilable", meaning incapable of being brought into agreement or harmony; unable to be reconciled. (असंगत / जिनमें मेल न हो सके)

◦ Correct: They may vary and seem very different, but they are not irreconcilable.

• Spelling key: IR + RE + CON + CIL + ABLE (double "r", then "reconcile" + "-able").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "irrecincilable", "irrecosilable" and "ireconcilable" (single "r") are all incorrect.

NOTE

• Built from "reconcile" (to make compatible) + prefix "ir-" (not) + suffix "-able". Related: reconcilable, reconciliation.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The table looks proper in the centre than in the corner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. more proper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" signals a comparison between two places (the centre vs the corner), so the comparative degree is required. As "proper" is a two-syllable adjective, its comparative is "more proper".

◦ Correct: The table looks more proper in the centre than in the corner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most proper" is the superlative, used for three or more, not with "than".

• Option 2 "properer" is not a standard form.

• Option 3 "properly" is an adverb and does not fit the comparison.

NOTE

• Longer adjectives form the comparative with "more ... than" and the superlative with "the most": more proper than / the most proper.

question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Along with his friend, he walked till the end of the street and came back immediately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he walked to the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Till" is used for time, not for distance/place. To show movement up to a place, we use "to". So "walked till the end" should be "walked to the end".

◦ Correct: Along with his friend, he walked to the end of the street and came back immediately.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "for came back immediately" and Option 3 "Near with his friend," are grammatically wrong.

• Option 4 "end by the street" changes the meaning incorrectly.

NOTE

• "Till/until" = up to a point of time (wait till evening); "to" = up to a place/point in space (walked to the end). "Up to" can be used for both.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Odious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Repugnant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Odious" means extremely unpleasant, hateful or repulsive. Its closest synonym is "repugnant" (causing strong dislike/disgust). (घृणित / अत्यंत अप्रिय)

◦ Example: Everyone condemned his odious/repugnant behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Pleasant", 2 "Acceptable" and 4 "Beautiful" are antonyms of odious.

NOTE

• Synonyms of odious: repugnant, hateful, detestable, abhorrent, loathsome. Antonyms: pleasant, agreeable, delightful, lovely.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has been travelling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "since the age of 16" (a starting point) with an action continuing into the present requires the present perfect continuous tense: "has been + verb-ing". As the subject "Hyojeng" is singular third person, we use "has".

◦ Correct: Hyojeng ... has been travelling since the age of 16.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "have been travelling" wrongly uses "have" for a singular subject.

• Option 1 "would have travelled" (past conditional) and Option 4 "will be travelling" (future) do not suit "since the age of 16".

NOTE

• Present perfect continuous with "since + point of time" shows an action that began in the past and is still continuing (She has been living here since 2015).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has covered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "So far" (up to now) signals the present perfect tense. The active present perfect for a singular subject is "has + past participle": "has covered" around twenty-five countries.

◦ Correct: She has covered around twenty-five countries so far.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will have covered" is future perfect (wrong time frame).

• Options 3 "had been covered" and 4 "was covered" are passive forms; here the action is active (she covers the countries).

NOTE

• "So far", "up to now", "till now", "recently" are time expressions that usually take the present perfect tense.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Visiting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank begins a sentence acting as the subject (a gerund/gerund phrase). "Visiting India was high on her wish list" — here "Visiting India" (a gerund phrase) works as the subject of "was". (गेरुंड — क्रिया का संज्ञा रूप)

◦ Correct: Visiting India was high on her wish list.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Visit" (base verb) cannot start this subject phrase correctly.

• Options 3 "Moved" and 4 "Moving" change the meaning; the passage is about visiting/travelling, not moving/relocating.

NOTE

• A gerund (verb + -ing) can act as the subject of a sentence: "Swimming is good exercise", "Reading helps the mind".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. explore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "planning to" is followed by the base form (infinitive without extra changes) of the verb: "planning to explore". So the blank takes "explore".

◦ Correct: ... planning to explore more of this beautiful city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "to be explored" is passive and creates "planning to to be explored", which is wrong.

• Option 3 "exploring" and Option 4 "having explored" do not follow "planning to" correctly.

NOTE

• "Plan to + base verb" (plan to travel, plan to explore). The infinitive marker "to" is already present, so only the base verb follows.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Hyojeng, a twenty-five-year-old South Korean Youtuber (1)_________since the age of 16. She (2)_______around twenty-five countries so far. (3)________ India was high on her wish list. She is currently soaking in the energy of Mumbai and planning to (4)________ more of this beautiful city. Unfortunately, her experience of the city turned sour recently. She was filming on the streets of Mumbai and two men tried to hug and kiss her, which was captured in her video. The video (5)_________ viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. went.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage narrates a past event ("She was filming ... two men tried to hug ..."), so the verb must be in the simple past. "The video went viral" is the correct past-tense form. (go – went – gone)

◦ Correct: The video went viral and the Mumbai police swung into action.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "going" and Option 4 "gone" cannot stand alone as the main verb without an auxiliary.

• Option 3 "go" is the present base form and does not match the past narration.

NOTE

• "Go viral" is a fixed expression meaning to spread quickly on the internet. Past: went viral; present perfect: has gone viral.

question: Which Chapter of Part VI of the Indian Constitution is concerned with the State Legislatures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chapter III.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the States, and its Chapter III is concerned with the State Legislature. (भाग VI, अध्याय III — राज्य विधानमंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Structure of Part VI (Articles 152–237): Chapter I – General; Chapter II – The Executive (Governor, Council of Ministers); Chapter III – The State Legislature (Articles 168–212); Chapter IV – Legislative power of the Governor; Chapter V – The High Courts; Chapter VI – Subordinate Courts.

• The State Legislature consists of the Governor, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, where it exists, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).

NOTE

• Part V deals with the Union (Parliament); Part VI deals with the States. Jammu & Kashmir earlier had special provisions, now reorganised as UTs.

question: Which of the following dance forms is inspired by the sculptures of the ancient temple of Chidambaram?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam is inspired by the sculptures of the ancient Nataraja (Thillai) temple of Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu, whose walls depict the 108 karanas (dance poses) of Lord Shiva. (भरतनाट्यम — चिदंबरम मंदिर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• The Chidambaram temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja (the cosmic dancer).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of urban population in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, among the given options, Mizoram has the highest percentage of urban population (about 52%). (मिज़ोरम — सर्वाधिक शहरी जनसंख्या प्रतिशत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Among all States/UTs, the NCT of Delhi (about 97.5%) and Goa (62%) had very high urban percentages; among the given four options, Mizoram leads.

• Tamil Nadu (about 48%), Maharashtra (about 45%) and Gujarat (about 43%) follow.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the first synchronous census was in 1881 and the 2011 census was the 15th. It is carried out by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

question: In Jain Basti temple of Karnataka, over the garbhagriha is raised a __________ storied nirandhara vimana with a square griva and sikhara.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Jain Basti temple of Karnataka, over the garbhagriha (sanctum) is raised a five-storied nirandhara vimana with a square griva and sikhara. (जैन बस्ती मंदिर — पाँच मंज़िला विमान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Garbhagriha" is the innermost sanctum housing the main deity; "vimana" is the tower over the sanctum (in South Indian/Dravidian temple architecture).

• A "nirandhara" temple is one without a circumambulatory path (pradakshina) around the sanctum; "griva" and "sikhara" are the neck and crowning part of the tower.

NOTE

• Basti/Basadi refers to a Jain temple in Karnataka. Karnataka has famous Jain sites like Shravanabelagola (the Gomateshwara/Bahubali statue).

question: With which of the following festivals does the five-day long festival of Diwali end?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhai Dooj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The five-day long festival of Diwali ends with "Bhai Dooj" (also called Bhai Bij/Bhaiya Dooj), which celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. (भाई दूज — दीवाली का अंतिम दिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The five days of Diwali in order: Day 1 – Dhanteras, Day 2 – Narak Chaturdashi (Chhoti Diwali), Day 3 – Lakshmi Puja (main Diwali), Day 4 – Govardhan Puja/Annakut, Day 5 – Bhai Dooj.

• Diwali, the festival of lights, marks the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya and the worship of Goddess Lakshmi.

NOTE

• Bhai Dooj is similar in spirit to Raksha Bandhan — both celebrate the brother–sister relationship.

question: In 1974, MS Subbulakshmi became the first Indian musician to win _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramon Magsaysay Award.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1974, the legendary Carnatic vocalist M. S. Subbulakshmi became the first Indian musician to win the Ramon Magsaysay Award. (एम.एस. सुब्बुलक्ष्मी — रेमन मैग्सेसे पुरस्कार, 1974)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• M. S. Subbulakshmi was also the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna (1998), India's highest civilian award.

• The Ramon Magsaysay Award is often called the "Nobel Prize of Asia", named after a former President of the Philippines.

NOTE

• Other notable Indian Magsaysay laureates: Vinoba Bhave, Mother Teresa, Jayaprakash Narayan, Verghese Kurien, Kiran Bedi, Arvind Kejriwal and Ravish Kumar.

question: Seleucus Nicator was a contemporary of ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chanakya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seleucus Nicator, a general of Alexander, was a contemporary of Chandragupta Maurya and his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya). Among the given options, Chanakya is correct. (सेल्यूकस निकेटर — चाणक्य का समकालीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Around 305 BCE, Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator, who then ceded territories and sent his ambassador Megasthenes to the Mauryan court; Megasthenes wrote "Indica".

• Chanakya was the chief adviser of Chandragupta and author of the "Arthashastra", a treatise on statecraft and economics.

NOTE

• The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya (321 BCE) with the guidance of Chanakya; its greatest ruler was Ashoka the Great.

question: With which of the following Amendment Acts of the Indian Constitution was 11th Fundamental Duty added?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 86th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. It makes it the duty of every parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child (aged 6–14 years). (86वाँ संविधान संशोधन — 11वाँ मूल कर्तव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The original 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, in Article 51A (Part IVA).

• The 86th Amendment (2002) also inserted Article 21A, making elementary education a Fundamental Right.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties were borrowed from the erstwhile USSR (Soviet) Constitution. They are non-justiciable (cannot be enforced by courts).

question: In November 2023, who was re-appointed as the Chairman of the Armed Forces Tribunal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Rajendra Menon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Justice Rajendra Menon was re-appointed as the Chairperson of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT). (जस्टिस राजेंद्र मेनन — सशस्त्र बल अधिकरण के अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) was established under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007, and began functioning in 2009. Its principal bench is in New Delhi.

• It adjudicates disputes and complaints regarding commission, appointments, service conditions and court-martial of personnel of the Army, Navy and Air Force.

NOTE

• Justice Sharad Arvind Bobde was the 47th Chief Justice of India; Justice N. V. Ramana was the 48th CJI; Justice R. F. Nariman was a former Supreme Court judge.

question: Neville Steven Joseph D'Souza is associated with which game?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Neville Stephen D'Souza was a famous Indian footballer. He is remembered for scoring a hat-trick at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics (against Australia), becoming the first Asian to score a hat-trick at the Olympics. (नेविल डिसूजा — फुटबॉल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the 1956 Melbourne Olympics, the Indian football team finished fourth, its best-ever Olympic performance, under coach Syed Abdul Rahim.

• India's football is governed by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

NOTE

• The 1950s–60s are called the "Golden Era of Indian Football", with stars like Neville D'Souza, PK Banerjee, Chuni Goswami and Tulsidas Balaram.

question: Which of the two following countries were formed as a result of the partition of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India and Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Partition of India in 1947 led to the creation of two independent dominions — India and Pakistan. (भारत का विभाजन — भारत और पाकिस्तान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The partition was based on the Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) and given effect by the Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament.

• Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947 and India on 15 August 1947. Sir Cyril Radcliffe drew the boundary line (the Radcliffe Line).

NOTE

• Bangladesh was formed later, in 1971, after separating from Pakistan (the erstwhile East Pakistan) following the Bangladesh Liberation War.

question: 'Straight from the Heart' is an autobiography of the famous cricketer ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kapil Dev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Straight from the Heart" is the autobiography of the legendary all-rounder Kapil Dev, who captained India to its first Cricket World Cup victory in 1983. (कपिल देव की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kapil Dev was the first bowler to take 400 Test wickets and was named the "Indian Cricketer of the Century" by Wisden in 2002.

• He received the Padma Bhushan and the Arjuna and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna awards.

NOTE

• Autobiographies of cricketers: Sunny Days (Sunil Gavaskar), Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh).

question: What is the stump height of a cricket wicket as per international standards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28 inches.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per international (MCC/ICC) standards, the height of the stumps in a cricket wicket is 28 inches (71.1 cm) above the ground. (स्टंप की ऊँचाई — 28 इंच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The overall width of the wicket (three stumps together, including the bails) is 9 inches (22.86 cm).

• The pitch length between the two sets of stumps is 22 yards (20.12 m).

NOTE

• Cricket's laws are maintained by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC); the international governing body is the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered in Dubai.

question: The Permanent Settlement introduced by Cornwallis was NOT prevalent in which of the following regions of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Permanent Settlement (1793), introduced by Lord Cornwallis, was NOT implemented in Punjab. It was mainly applied to Bengal, Bihar and Odisha (and later parts of the North). (स्थायी बंदोबस्त — पंजाब में लागू नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) fixed the land revenue permanently and made the zamindars the owners of land.

• Other land revenue systems: the Ryotwari System (Thomas Munro & Reed) in Madras/Bombay, and the Mahalwari System (Holt Mackenzie/William Bentinck) in the North-West Provinces and Punjab.

NOTE

• Lord Cornwallis is also called the "Father of Civil Services in India" for reforming the administrative and judicial systems.

question: According to the advancing of monsoon in India, which of the following cities receives rainfall after 15 June every year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As the southwest monsoon advances over India, Jaipur (Rajasthan) — being in the north-west — receives its rainfall relatively late, generally after 15 June. (जयपुर — 15 जून के बाद मानसून)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The southwest monsoon normally arrives over Kerala around 1 June, reaches the north-east and southern peninsula early, and progresses towards the north-west (Rajasthan, Punjab) by mid-July.

• Imphal, Bengaluru and Hyderabad lie in the east/south and receive monsoon rains earlier than Jaipur.

NOTE

• India gets about 75% of its annual rainfall from the southwest monsoon (June–September). The monsoon withdraws (retreats) from the north-west by early September.

question: Which of the following sultans of Delhi set up three different markets for different commodities in Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alauddin Khalji set up different markets (mandis) for different commodities in Delhi and introduced strict market/price control regulations. (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी — बाज़ार नियंत्रण व्यवस्था)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• His main markets included the Grain Market (Mandi), the Cloth Market (Sarai Adl) and the market for horses, slaves and cattle.

• He appointed a Shahna-i-Mandi (market superintendent) and intelligence officers (barids) to control prices — mainly to maintain a large, cheap standing army against Mongol invasions.

NOTE

• Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296–1316) of the Khalji dynasty was a powerful ruler; his generals Malik Kafur led campaigns into South India.

question: Who among the following dancers won the prestigious Padma Shree award in the year 2021, for her contribution to folk dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Matha B Manjamma Jogathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Matha B. Manjamma Jogathi, a folk dancer from Karnataka, won the Padma Shri in 2021 for her contribution to Jogati Nritya (folk dance). She is a transgender folk artist and former President of the Karnataka Janapada Academy. (मंजम्मा जोगती — पद्म श्री 2021)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, given for distinguished contribution in various fields.

• Jogati Nritya is a traditional folk dance form associated with the worship of Goddess Yellamma (Renuka) in North Karnataka.

NOTE

• The four Padma/civilian awards in order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

question: Which state government of India launched the 'Swanirbhar Nari' aimed at making the weavers of the state self-reliant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Assam government launched the "Swanirbhar Nari" scheme to make the weavers of the state self-reliant by directly purchasing their handloom products and eliminating middlemen. (स्वनिर्भर नारी — असम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Swanirbhar Nari" means "self-reliant woman"; the scheme empowers women weavers economically.

• Assam is famous for its handloom and silk — especially Muga, Eri and Pat silk. Sualkuchi in Assam is called the "Manchester of the East".

NOTE

• Assam: Capital – Dispur; famous for tea gardens, Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhino) and the Brahmaputra river.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India governs the Population Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 246.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 246 of the Constitution governs the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and States through the Seventh Schedule. The "Census" is listed as Entry 69 of the Union List, so it is governed under Article 246. (अनुच्छेद 246 — जनगणना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Census is a Union subject, conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Census Act, 1948.

• The Seventh Schedule has three lists: Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

NOTE

• Article 179 – vacation/resignation of the Speaker/Deputy Speaker of a State Assembly; Article 233 – appointment of District Judges; Article 128 – attendance of retired judges at Supreme Court sittings.

question: Bhakra Dam is built on which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satluj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhakra Dam is built on the Satluj (Sutlej) River in Himachal Pradesh. It is one of the highest gravity dams in the world. (भाखड़ा बाँध — सतलुज नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bhakra–Nangal Project is a joint venture of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan; the reservoir formed is called the "Gobind Sagar Lake".

• Jawaharlal Nehru called such multipurpose river valley projects the "Temples of Modern India".

NOTE

• The Satluj is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab; the five rivers are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Satluj (tributaries of the Indus).

question: The zone where the earthquake waves are not observed is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shadow Zone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The area on the Earth's surface where seismic (earthquake) waves are not recorded by seismographs is called the "Shadow Zone". (छाया क्षेत्र — जहाँ भूकंप तरंगें दर्ज नहीं होतीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• P-waves (primary) are longitudinal and travel through solids, liquids and gases; S-waves (secondary) are transverse and travel only through solids.

• The S-wave shadow zone (beyond 105° from the epicentre) proves that the outer core is liquid, as S-waves cannot pass through it.

NOTE

• The "hypocentre/focus" is the point of origin inside the Earth; the "epicentre" is the point directly above it on the surface. Earthquakes are measured on the Richter scale.

question: Identify the primary characteristic of the Cooperative Development Foundation (CDF) model of SHGs regarding its focus on membership from the following.
option_3: It includes both poor and non-poor members.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It includes both poor and non-poor members.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cooperative Development Foundation (CDF) model of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) is characterised by an inclusive membership — it includes both poor and non-poor members rather than targeting only one group. (CDF मॉडल — निर्धन व गैर-निर्धन दोनों सदस्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CDF, based in Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, promoted thrift and credit cooperatives among rural people, emphasising self-reliance and savings.

• Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are small, voluntary associations (usually 10–20 members) that pool savings and give small loans to members.

NOTE

• The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in 1992 to connect SHGs with formal banking and promote financial inclusion.

question: The number of organisms in the population divided by a regular unit of area or volume is called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is population density.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Population density" is defined as the number of organisms (individuals) in a population divided by a unit of area or volume (e.g., number per square kilometre). (जनसंख्या घनत्व = व्यक्तियों की संख्या ÷ क्षेत्रफल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Birth rate (natality) is the number of births per unit population per unit time; death rate (mortality) is the number of deaths per unit population per unit time.

• Population size simply refers to the total number of individuals in a population, without reference to area.

NOTE

• As per Census 2011, India's average population density was 382 persons per sq km; Bihar was the most densely populated state.

question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.
option_2: Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This statement is INCORRECT. In reality, boiling is a bulk phenomenon (it occurs throughout the liquid at the boiling point), while evaporation is a surface phenomenon (it occurs only at the surface, at any temperature). (उबलना — बल्क; वाष्पीकरण — सतही परिघटना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Evaporation happens at all temperatures and occurs only at the surface of the liquid.

• Boiling happens at a fixed temperature (boiling point) and occurs throughout the entire body (bulk) of the liquid.

• Evaporation causes cooling because the particles that escape carry away energy (latent heat), lowering the temperature of the remaining liquid.

NOTE

• The rate of evaporation increases with higher temperature, larger surface area, lower humidity and more wind speed.

question: The iodine value of oil and fat indicates:
solution_text:
The correct answer is degree of unsaturation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "iodine value (or iodine number)" of an oil or fat indicates the degree of unsaturation — i.e., the number of carbon–carbon double bonds present. A higher iodine value means more unsaturation. (आयोडीन मान — असंतृप्तता की मात्रा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is measured as the grams of iodine absorbed by 100 grams of the fat/oil; iodine adds across the double bonds.

• Unsaturated fats/oils (like vegetable oils) have high iodine values, while saturated fats (like butter/ghee) have low iodine values.

NOTE

• Unsaturated oils are generally liquid at room temperature and considered healthier; they can be converted to solid fats (like vanaspati) by hydrogenation, which reduces the iodine value.
